hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-ACS: Such profiles have been taken in Danish waters: Gonçalves-Araujo and Markager (2020) mounted an AC-S spectrophotometer on the CTD frame at stations of the national monitoring programme (NOVANA) around Fyn, in autumn 2017 and spring 2019, and call the instrument's incorporation into the sampling programme in 2017 a first step toward automated, sensor-based monitoring.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-ACSGAP: None of the CTD extract's `Parameter` values is an absorption, so no such profile reaches the extract this project holds; until one does, the shrinkage test is joint with a spectral model.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-CTDPARAM: **CTD channels.** The CTD extract carries `Lysdæmpning` on 5,217,377 rows, `Fluorescens` on 6,783,790, `Turbiditet` on 1,076,915 and `FDOM` on 890,921, with `Photometer måling` on 576,179 and `Photometer reference` on 531,071 beside them.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-EACHFAIL: Each can fail: the ordering would leave Z8's attribution complaint empty here, the constant would make the fixed constant harmless, and the artefact would refute the spectral reading of the light analysis.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-FDOMSPAN: `FDOM` runs only from 2021 to 2026, so a test on both composition channels is confined to those years; before them the extract holds no other channel for dissolved organic matter.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-FIT: Require the fit coefficient: the instruction forbids reporting a Kd converted from Secchi depth as a Kd value (*må ikke indrapporteres til databasen som Kd-værdier*), and a fitted correlation shows a record came from a profile, so a record that broke the rule cannot enter.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-HALF: Z8 says Denmark measures broadband Kd, *which cannot be partitioned even in principle*. The first half is the protocol's own rule; the second holds for the number alone, but the missing partition is set **by protocol**, not by physics, and the archive holds, on the same casts, channels the protocol does not use.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-LYS: **Light profiles.** `lys.csv.gz` holds 2,370,091 records at 566 stations with a position; this project's light analysis counts 62,741 casts in it with a positive Kd and a date, 60,697 of them with a fit correlation of at least 0.9 or none reported.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-LYSCOLS: Each record carries the depths its regression used, `ZMin` and `ZMax` — the instruction's *øverste* and *nederst dybde som er anvendt* — and its correlation coefficient: Kd is a regression the operator fitted over a window the operator chose, a profile collapsed to one slope.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-M06: The governing method document is DCE's technical instruction `M06` *Lyssvækkelse* by Markager and Fossing, version 3, valid from 04.06.2015 ([PDF](https://ecos.au.dk/fileadmin/ecos/Fagdatacentre/Marin/TA_M06_Lyssvaekkelse_ver3.pdf)):
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-M06-BED: It also sets aside the readings nearest the bed where sediment is stirred up from the bottom (*Nederst i vandsøjlen kan sediment hvirvles op fra bunden*), and it leaves which readings to drop to the fitter's experience: *Der kan ikke gives præcise anvisninger til denne procedure*.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-M06-FACTOR: Section `2.5.2`: in Danish waters the empirical constant converting Secchi depth to Kd varies between 1.5 and 3.6, but can be as low as 0.6 in very turbid systems where scattering matters, and up to 4.1 where dissolved matter dominates the attenuation; in practice it is set to 2.3.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-M06-PAR: One band, mandated: *skal der måles fotosyntetisk aktivt lys i intervallet* 400–700 *nm også kaldet PAR* — photosynthetically active light, one broad band.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-M06-SPEC: Section `2.5.1` names the spectral mechanism and prescribes deletion as the cure: *Lysets spektrale sammensætning og spredning ændrer sig med vanddybden … en ikke-lineær hældning. I disse tilfælde kan det være nødvendigt at udelade lysmålinger fra den nederste del af vandsøjlen* — the light's spectrum changes with depth, the log-transformed profile can bend, and the lowest readings may then be left out.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-MATCH: The satellite arm's null is built on the matched subset: `matchup.py` records, from its first run, that casts with a same-day satellite retrieval are clearer than the rest in the same months, so the matched days are not a random sample of days.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-NOCLOCK: Over all of it, the extract has no wavelength column and no time of day.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-NULL: Not a regression's nominal F-null. Casts are clustered by station, seasonal and autocorrelated, and the composition channels share a station's mean level with Kd. **Permute the composition channels together, one row per cast, across casts within station × calendar month**, preserving each channel's marginals and the station/season structure, and rebuild the apportionment 1,000 times; the observed unique variance must beat that distribution. Same permutation for the constant and the artefact; the result is whatever the permutation returns, reported even when it exceeds the observed statistic.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-P-ART: **The artefact.** The apparent-Kd decline with depth — in this project's light analysis the median ratio of lower-half to upper-half Kd is 0.879 for profiles starting between 0 and 0.6 m, rising to 0.987 for those starting below 5.1 m — **weakens as FDOM rises**, because absorption by coloured dissolved organic matter at short wavelengths narrows the spread of K(λ) across the PAR band that produces the decline. The sign is the prediction; the magnitude needs an assumed K(λ) and is not part of the test.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-P-CONST: **The constant.** `Kd · z_Secchi` on the same station-day varies with FDOM and turbidity after station and month are removed. The instruction's own range predicts this; its fixed constant denies it.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-P-ORDER: **Ordering.** Ranking casts by the chlorophyll proxy does not reproduce the ranking by Kd, and casts above a Kd threshold fall into distinct composition types — high-FDOM/low-turbidity and high-turbidity/low-FDOM — rather than one.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-PERCAST: Per **cast** — never a water body, which is why the area files `val_kd.bin` and `val_secchi.bin`, one value per coastal water body (`DKCOAST…`) and month, cannot serve here.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-PROXY: Errors in the proxies: `ppb` and `FTU` are sensor units, not absorption coefficients; FDOM is fluorescence (fluorescent dissolved organic matter), not absorption by coloured dissolved organic matter; and turbidity is light scattered at right angles, not absorption by non-algal particles.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-RANGE: That range **is** the partition: the constant moves with what attenuates the light, so fixing it assumes the composition away.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-REFIT: The photometer channels — a reading and a reference, in the photon-flux unit the instruction gives for surface light — look like the underwater and surface sensors its fit is made from, one value per depth row. If they are, Kd can be refitted over a *stated* window instead of the operator's, on the same cast as the composition channels. The reading channel has more rows than the reference, so not every reading has its reference.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-S1: Cast table from `lys.csv.gz` via `formats.num()`: station, date, Kd, fit, `ZMin`, `ZMax`; keep casts with a fit coefficient.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-S2: Stream `ctd.csv.gz` once, cast-contiguous (flush on key change, count reopened keys), emitting per station and date the depth-median `Fluorescens`, `FDOM` and `Turbiditet` **over `ZMin…ZMax`** — the layer the Kd was fitted over, not the whole cast.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-S3: Inner-join on station and date; report how the joined subset differs from all light casts in Kd, station and month — that selection is the first result.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-S4: Apportion Kd's variance among the proxies within station × month, then fit the ordering and the constant against `maaledybde.csv.gz` Secchi on the same station-day, and the artefact — each against the permutation null below, reported as a distribution rather than a p-value. Repeat with satellite absorption and backscatter retrievals where one reaches back before the FDOM record.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SATSPLIT: The satellite arm cannot split dissolved matter from detritus: its absorption term for them (`adg`) is one combined coefficient.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SEARCH: Beyond these, the source register records searches of PANGAEA and of that product for spectral absorption in Danish water, with a Roskilde Fjord series as the only positive: an absence over those searches, *not a finding that none exists*.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SHRINK: A residual is testable only by measuring a part out of it and checking that it shrinks by exactly that part — which needs absorption in units: a spectrophotometer or spectroradiometer profile beside the PAR cast.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SONDE: `SondeNr` is the placeholder `999`, probe unknown, on 25.6% of the CTD extract's rows, so on those rows the probe, and any calibration tied to it, cannot be identified.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SRC-131: **Copernicus Marine [`OCEANCOLOUR_BAL_BGC_L3_NRT_009_131`](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/OCEANCOLOUR_BAL_BGC_L3_NRT_009_131/description)** — near-real-time daily observations from OLCI at 300 m, with an optics dataset of absorption and backscatter by dissolved and particulate matter and by phytoplankton (`ADG`, `APH`, `BBP`) from the QAA model; its catalogue record starts in 2023.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SRC-133: The Baltic multiyear product already fetched, `OCEANCOLOUR_BAL_BGC_L3_MY_009_133`, names plankton, reflectances and transparency in its title and no optics, where its near-real-time sibling's title adds optics.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SRC-208: **Copernicus Marine [`OCEANCOLOUR_BAL_BGC_HR_L4_NRT_009_208`](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/OCEANCOLOUR_BAL_BGC_HR_L4_NRT_009_208/description)** — `Sentinel-2` MSI at 100 m for a 20 km coastal zone: turbidity, suspended matter, particulate backscatter (`BBP443`) and chlorophyll, and no absorption variable; its catalogue record starts in 2020.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SRC-CCI: **ESA Ocean Colour CCI inherent optical properties, `v6.0`** ([CEDA](https://catalogue.ceda.ac.uk/uuid/024292dcda5d42ceb326850f89f8b40d/)) — global, at approximately 4 km, in composites from daily to yearly, covering 1997 to 2022: total absorption and backscatter, and absorption by detrital and dissolved matter and by phytoplankton, the dissolved-and-detrital term from the QAA model.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SRC-CTD: **Held: the CTD extract's light and composition channels**, per depth. **Not a separate path** from the light profiles: the instruction says the light sensor is usually mounted on the CTD (*sædvanligvis monteret på CTD’en*).
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SRC-MODIS: **NASA Aqua MODIS `L3` inherent optical properties, version `2022.0`** ([Earthdata](https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/data/catalog/ob-cloud-modisa-l3m-iop-2022.0)) — retrieved with the GIOP model framework, not QAA: phytoplankton absorption and combined CDOM and detritus absorption (`aph_443`, `adg_443`), from 2002.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SRC-PATH: Every satellite product above is a retrieval of optical properties from reflectance — a model applied to radiometry from orbit — so each is a separate production path from the ship's casts, and none is a measurement of absorption in the water.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-STATUS: The test this page specifies has not been run: no script in this repository computes it.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-SUM: `Kd = K_water + K_phyto + K_CDOM + K_NAP`. On the in-situ arm **none of the terms is in absorption units**, so this yields a variance apportionment, not a budget, and the residual holds the start-depth artefact, the operator's window choice and the time of day.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-UNITS: The unit column, `Enhed`, says what they are, by count: `FTU` stands on 1,076,915 rows, exactly as many as `Turbiditet`; `ppb` on 890,921, as many as `FDOM`; `µmol fotoner/(m2*sek)` on 1,107,250, as many as the photometer channels together (1,107,250); and `pct` on 11,815,696, as many as `Lysdæmpning` and oxygen saturation (`Oxygenmætning`) together (11,815,696). So turbidity and FDOM are in sensor units and the photometers in photon flux, and `Lysdæmpning` is a percentage — matching the instruction's light value in the water column as a percentage of surface irradiance (*lysværdi i vandsøjlen i procent af overfladeindstråling*), not its attenuation coefficient, whose unit is per metre.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-WINDOW: Leaving out the lowest readings deletes the mineral signal a partition wants, and where a fit's profile starts matters: this project's light analysis finds the median depth at which light falls to 11% of the surface at 6.31 m in casts whose shallowest reading lies above 2 m, against 8.18 m in those starting deeper.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-WOULD: **Would:** a statement about the *record* — whether Kd's cast-to-cast variance at named stations in named months is carried mainly by the chlorophyll channel, against a permutation null, and whether the instruction's fixed constant of 2.3 is composition-free.
hypodrafts/Z8.md.C-DZ-Z8-WOULDNOT: **Would not:** a physical budget, a causal attribution, any per-water-body or national number, or any trend.

openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-AL561: **AL561** (GEOMAR, 2021): benthic landers and cores at high-accumulation sites in the Skagerrak and Kattegat; the chamber record at station `AL561_17-1` lists phosphate and ammonium among its measured nutrients, and the source register records the cruise's stations reaching from the Kattegat to the Skagerrak, several of them nearer Sweden or Norway.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-ASYM: **That asymmetry is the problem.** The response side has ortho-phosphate at 650 stations in the held extract; the pool side has 39 stations in the entire national record as the portal lists it.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-CHAMBERFORM: The **chamber form breaks it completely** and is the only thing that isolates the bed; the in-situ chamber fluxes found for Danish inner waters are one cruise's.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-DIP: The response side: the held water-chemistry extract carries `Ortho-phosphat-P` on 182,070 samples that `scripts/rescore.py` accepts, at 650 stations over 1970-2026. Below its depth cut the monthly median runs from 17.0 µg/l in April, the lowest month, to 28.0 µg/l in October, the highest.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-DIPFORM: The **DIP-seasonality form breaks it.** It sets one directly observed quantity (summer minus winter ortho-phosphate near the bed) against another (loss on ignition and iron-adsorbed P at the same position). No budget is closed, nothing is a remainder. The price is that it is **weak**: a summer DIP rise over organic-rich bed is equally consistent with water-column regeneration co-located with it, since deposition drives both. It can *falsify* the benthic signature - no covariance means A7 leaves no mark at station resolution - but a positive result does not isolate the bed.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-DISCREP: ODA's portal lists 39 Sedimentkemi/Sporstof stations ever. Either that rotation has not run long or ODA does not expose the whole record, and which is not established here. Ask before quoting either number.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-FR483: **NERI Technical Report `483`** (Fossing et al. 2004) sets up an oxygen and nutrient flux model for Aarhus Bay. Its constants were set by comparing the model's stationary state with a year's mean measurements from the HAV90 programme in Aarhus Bay, and it cites that programme's reports on the sea floor's oxygen uptake (Gundersen et al. 1995) and nitrogen cycling (Lomstein and Blackburn 1992).
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-HYLEN: **Hylén et al. (2025)**, *In situ-measured benthic fluxes of dissolved inorganic phosphorus in the Baltic Sea* (Earth System Science Data), publish 498 DIP fluxes measured in situ with benthic chamber landers at 59 stations between 2001 and 2021, with bottom-water oxygen, sediment organic carbon and sediment type beside them. The data are one file, `BalticSeaInSituFluxDIP_v3.xlsx`, in Zenodo record `17465937`, under the Creative Commons Attribution licence.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-HYLEN-PATH: A chamber lander incubating a patch of bed is a different instrument, quantity and operator from the CTD sonde - the authors are at the University of Gothenburg, GEOMAR and elsewhere, not Danish monitoring - so it is a production path separate from the CTD, ocean colour and Secchi.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-HYLEN-WEST: They do not count the Kattegat and the Belt Sea, west of the Arkona Basin, as part of the Baltic Sea, and the westernmost subbasin they group is the Arkona and Bornholm Basin, so no station of theirs lies in the Kattegat or the Belts.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-JANFEB: **The January–February sampling is why the residual keeps reappearing.** The pool is measured once a year, in winter; the release is claimed for summer. With one annual observation the summer drawdown *cannot* be a difference of two measurements, so anyone wanting a number must infer it. The programme design forces model-as-datum here.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-MD: `data/raw/oda/maaledybde.csv.gz` - 151,203 records at 1,429 stations, 1,176 of them carrying `BundDybde_m`. **Its northing is missing:** the second easting column `X_UTM321` repeats `X_UTM32` in 151,203 of the 151,203 records. Positions come from `stations_series`, not from it.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-NOVANA: **An unresolved discrepancy, flagged not settled.** The national programme for 2023–2027 takes sediment nutrient pools - total N, total P, iron-bound phosphate, dry matter, loss on ignition and density - once a year, when the sediment is most oxidised, in January–February, from 90 of the 109 water bodies over the period, at 16–19 stations a year; its table gives 17–19 stations a year.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-ODA: **ODA Vandkemi** (`Emne_10_11`) is held; **Sedimentkemi** (`Emne_12_19`), with loss on ignition, total N and P and iron-adsorbed P by layer, is not. Bottle chemistry is a production path separate from the CTD sonde.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-PANEL: `docs/data/areas/stations_series.json` - 679,422 station-months, 1,415 stations, 564 months from 1980, 9 variables (`fluo` 60,460 · `oxy_bed` 76,980 · `oxy_surf` 76,963 · `oxysat_bed` 64,493 · `oxysat_surf` 64,552 · `sal_bed` 83,309 · `sal_surf` 83,341 · `temp_bed` 84,656 · `temp_surf` 84,668). **No nutrient variable.**
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-POOL: The pool side, ODA's Sedimentkemi, is not held, so A7 cannot yet be scored in either form.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-PORTAL: The source register records the ODA portal's station lists, taken with an explicit period in an authenticated comparison: Vandkemi 1,125 stations over 1970–2026 against 205 with no period set; Sedimentkemi/Sporstof 39 over the whole record, 18 currently.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-RESID: Internal loading inferred as what a mass balance leaves over is model-as-datum by construction. FR483 is a local instance: a model of Aarhus Bay whose constants were fitted to a year's measured means.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-S1: **One fetch.** `Emne_12_19` (Sedimentkemi): 39 stations ever, and it fixes how many positions the test can have. `scripts/fetch_oda.py` has no entry for it: its `TOPICS` already carry the water chemistry `Emne_10_11`, and its argument parser accepts only those keys, so it is one entry more, the node id already recorded in `data/manual/data_sources.json`. Set an explicit period - the portal's station list is filtered by the period set, and returns the current network without one.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-S2: **Check the join before designing anything.** Count stations carrying *both* a sediment core and ≥5 years of monthly DIP within 2 km. If fewer than 10 do, the armchair classification is wrong and A7 is a measurement gap in both forms. Stating this in advance is the point.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-S3: **The measurement.** Sample the existing sediment stations **twice**, late February and late September, instead of once in winter. That change turns the summer release from a residual into a difference of two measured pools, at whatever station count is already funded. Then: one chamber deployment in the Kattegat, the Belts or a Danish fjord, where no chamber flux was found.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-SEABED: `data/raw/geus/seabed_sediment_dk.gpkg`, layer `Seabed_sedimen` - 108 polygons in 7 substrate classes (Gravel and coarse sand 22, Mud and sandy mud 9, Muddy sand 16, Quaternary clay and silt 14, Sand 22, Sedimentary rock 3, Till/diamicton 22), compiled from 22 named survey campaigns at map scales whose denominators run from 5,000 to 500,000. Usable as substrate class if the scale travels with it; **no organic-carbon value at all**, as the register's `R7-TOC-MAP-GAP` records.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-SR323: **DCE's SR323** tabulates the internal and external load of DIN and DIP for Roskilde, Odense, Horsens and Ringkøbing Fjord by three-month period from summer 1999 to spring 2000, credited to unpublished data by H. Fossing: a net annual release of phosphorus from the sediment in Roskilde, Odense and Horsens Fjord, a net uptake in Ringkøbing Fjord. It cites Kerteminde Fjord, where in 1991–1992 the sediment's release made up 65% and 70% of the total N and P load.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-SR323-DATA: The measurements behind the table were not found in any reachable dataset.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-STATUS: **Missing: armchair for the weak form, measurement for the strong form.** A7 says the bed releases stored N and P in summer. Its two discriminators fall in different categories:
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-STRONG: **benthic flux chambers** - for Danish inner waters the in-situ chamber fluxes found are one cruise's, in the Skagerrak and Kattegat in 2021; a seasonal internal load for four Danish fjords in 1999–2000 is tabulated from unpublished data, and the measurements behind it were not found. **Measurement.**
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-TA14: **NOVA teknisk anvisning `kap. 14`** (1998) specifies light and dark incubations of sediment cores for the fluxes of oxygen, ortho-phosphate, nitrate, nitrite, ammonium, urea and silicate, on type areas only.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-WEAK: **the DIP seasonality ratio against the sediment organic pool** - the response side is held and the pool side is in ODA, unfetched. **Armchair.** Tentative, not an obstacle.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-WOULD: **Would.** Whether near-bed phosphate seasonality covaries with bed organic content across positions, as a coefficient with its qualifiers.
openproblems/A7.md.C-OQ-A7-WOULDNOT: **Would not.** Any share, tonnage or "internal loading accounts for n%": that is a mass balance and this is not one. Nor anything about Danish inner waters from the Zenodo data, whose basins the paper defines as excluding the Kattegat and the Belt Sea - carrying them westward would be the aggregation error this project audits elsewhere.

openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-ARMCHAIR: Not yet **armchair**: an armchair block means the numbers exist and joining them is merely too large.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-CONFLATE: **Schema conflation.** One quality-element code stands for every river-basin-specific pollutant, whatever the substance, in a single column. A pesticide effect cannot be separated from any other pollutant's even in principle at this resolution.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-CTD: `data/raw/oda/ctd.csv.gz` - 53,710,760 records; the `Parameter` column takes 17 distinct values: Temperatur, Salinitet, Oxygen indhold, Fluorescens, Oxygenmætning, Lysdæmpning, Konduktivitet, Vægtfylde, Turbiditet, FDOM, Photometer måling, Photometer reference, pH, Strømhastighed, Strømretning, Farvestof, Dihydrogensulfid. **Not one is a pesticide, a degradation product, or any organic contaminant.**
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-GEUS: `data/raw/geus/` holds only `seabed_sediment_dk.gpkg` and `marta_sedimentproever.geojson` - a sediment **map** and raw-material samples. There is **no Jupiter groundwater chemistry** here.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-GW: The groundwater files in `data/raw/` - `grundvand_pejlinger_2021.geojson`, `grundvand_potentialelinjer_2021.geojson` and `terraen_minus_gvs.geojson` - hold water levels, potentiometric contours and depth to the water table, and no analyte. The groundwater route to a land-side pesticide series is not present in this archive.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-KEMI: `data/raw/oda/kemi.csv.gz`, the marine water chemistry with its hazardous substances, is held, and among its `Parameter` values are `Diuron` on 63 records, a herbicide, and `Hydroxy-atrazin` on 62 and `Hydroxysimazin` on 63, the hydroxy forms of the triazine herbicides atrazine and simazine; beside them two chlorinated phenoxypropionic acids, `2-(2,6-dichlorphenoxy)propionsyre` on 100 and `2-(2-Chlor-6-methylphenoxy)propionsyre` on 984, whose use this page has not checked.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-KEMI-THIN: The held counts are records per parameter; how many stations and years they span has not been counted, so whether they meet the test below is open.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-LEGACY: So pesticides do appear in the marine record - HCH, whose gamma isomer lindane has been used as an agricultural insecticide, in fish, and the herbicides above in the water - but whether any is dense enough to join against fauna is the test below, not yet run.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-LICENSE: Even a complete marine pesticide series would **not** license "pesticides did it". E7's own prediction is that pesticide and nitrogen load are collinear because one agriculture produces both, so a concentration series is only discriminating where the two vary independently - same nutrient load, different pesticide exposure. Whether that contrast exists anywhere in Danish waters is a second, unanswered measurement question, and it is worth answering *before* collecting the first series rather than after.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-LICENSE2: What the series would license immediately is narrower and still worth having: a statement of whether the exposure is present at concentrations near the effect thresholds of the conserved targets at all - which this project has not examined, for the held herbicide records or any other.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-MFS: `data/raw/national/sw_mfs_tilstand.geojson` - **256 points, none of them marine**: 152 `DKLAKE`, 104 `DKRIVER`. Matrices flagged: biota 253, water 174, **sediment 5**, nothing 3.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-MFS-ONE: What each point carries is `qecode = "QE3-3 - River Basin Specific Pollutants"`, `qestatusor = "3"`, `da_oekolog = "2"` and `aktivstart = 01-01-1999`, each the same on all 256. **No analyte name, no concentration, no unit, no sampling date.**
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-MFSTOPICS: The source register records the analyte lists of the ODA marine hazardous-substance topics: sediment (`ODA-SEDKEMI-MFS`) phthalates, alkylphenols and bulk carbon, and no pesticide; mussels (`ODA-MFS-MUSLING`) organotins, metals, PAH, dioxins and PCBs; fish (`ODA-MFS-FISK`) PFAS, brominated flame retardants, PCBs, dioxins, HCH, DDT and DDE, HCB and mercury.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-NEEDS: E7 says agricultural pesticides reach the sea and act on non-target organisms, and that they are collinear with nitrogen because the same farming produces both. Discriminating it needs, at shared positions: (a) a concentration of at least one **named** active substance or degradation product in water, sediment or biota; (b) a fauna or algal response; (c) a nutrient-load covariate to hold fixed.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-NOMARINE: No marine water body here carries a hazardous-substance observation: of the 123 marine water bodies, 0 have a point of the layer, because every point belongs to a lake or a river.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-NOTEXP: Not **experiment**: no intervention is required. Ordinary monitoring, of a kind already run for nutrients, would produce the series.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-PANEL: `docs/data/areas/stations_series.json` - 679,422 station-months, 1,415 stations, 564 monthly slots from 1980, across 9 variables: fluorescence, oxygen and oxygen saturation (bed and surface), salinity and temperature (bed and surface). **No toxicant variable of any kind.** Near-bed oxygen alone is 76,980 station-months over 1,327 stations: the response-side record is dense; the exposure side has no column to sit in there.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-PANELCHOICE: Pick the panel by target conservation, not market label: a photosystem-II inhibitor with its degradation product, since the algae the chlorophyll indicator counts photosynthesise, and glyphosate with AMPA, its breakdown product in soil.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-RECLASS: **Reclassification test, stated in advance.** If named pesticide or degradation-product analytes are found at ≥20 marine stations with ≥5 years of dated results and a non-censored fraction above 33%, E7 moves to **armchair** and this page is wrong. Anything thinner leaves it here.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-REG: `data/raw/oda/stations.csv` - the ODA station register: 798,574 rows, 6,288 distinct stations.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-S1: **Count, then enumerate.** In the held water chemistry, count stations and years for each pesticide parameter - that decides the test above for the water. Then run the topic and parameter *metadata* calls `scripts/fetch_oda.py` already implements (`expand`, `option_list`) against Hav / Sedimentkemi / MFS Sporstof and Hav / MFS i biota, and record the parameter names and per-parameter station counts. Metadata only, no extract.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-S2: **If that is too thin**, the smallest useful addition is one analyte panel bolted onto stations that already carry fauna: 20 existing `Bundfauna` stations spanning an agricultural gradient, sampled before application, twice after, and in winter, sediment plus passive samplers. The requirements, each of which the national pollutant-status layer violates: **named analytes reported individually, never a "pesticides" sum**; **per-analyte LOD reported with every result**, chosen below the effect concentration for the conserved target rather than wherever the instrument lands; and **"< LOD" recorded as censoring with its threshold**, so a non-detect is reportable as a bound instead of silently becoming a zero.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-SALES: No pesticide sales or usage series is held, and the source register records that where Denmark's national pesticide statistics are now published could not be established.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-SIDES: (a) is held, thinly, in the water chemistry. (b) is in ODA `Bundfauna`, not fetched. (c) is not held as a load: the water carries nutrient concentrations, but river load lives on an ODA endpoint `fetch_oda.py` cannot reach.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-STATUS: **Missing: measurement.** The quantity the hypothesis is about is held only thinly: the held marine water chemistry names a herbicide and two degradation products of herbicides, on 62 to 63 records each, and nothing held pairs them with a fauna response. E7 is **unscoreable here, not refuted**.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-STREAMS: The land-side series that does exist is ODA's stream water chemistry (`ODA-VANDLOEB-MFS`), which the source register records as carrying glyphosate, AMPA, bentazon, MCPA, mechlorprop and other pesticides per sample; it is not fetched.
openproblems/E7.md.C-OQ-E7-VERDICT: **Model-as-datum.** The value is a status verdict, and it is invariant across all 256 points, so it carries no information for discriminating anything.

openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-ASK: Cheaper still, and prerequisite to the first reason: **ask ODA for the path length of the instrument behind `Lysdæmpning`.** Without it no attenuation coefficient can be reconstructed from the channel's 5,217,377 records.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-CTDPARAMS: The CTD extract `data/raw/oda/ctd.csv.gz` carries 17 distinct `Parameter` values over its 53,710,760 records: Temperatur 7,501,421 · Salinitet 7,474,645 · Oxygen indhold 7,147,012 · Fluorescens 6,783,790 · Oxygenmætning 6,598,319 · Lysdæmpning 5,217,377 · Konduktivitet 5,169,432 · Vægtfylde 4,329,674 · Turbiditet 1,076,915 · FDOM 890,921 · Photometer måling 576,179 · Photometer reference 531,071 · pH 237,496 · Strømhastighed 84,734 · Strømretning 84,572 · Farvestof 4,601 · Dihydrogensulfid 2,601.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-DISC: J1 says gel production rises when the N:P ratio is skewed **in either direction**, and it names its own discriminator: TEP against the ambient N:P ratio and bloom senescence stage, not against nutrient load.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-FDOMUNIT: `FDOM`'s 890,921 records match the 890,921 in `ppb`, a concentration unit, not an absorption coefficient. The total has no dimension; the parts come from one column that mixes scales.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-LYSD: The per-depth `Lysdæmpning` channel escapes that artefact but inherits the first reason instead.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-NOSCRIPT: No script in this repository computes it.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-NOTEP: No TEP, no polysaccharide, no Alcian blue, no gel, no microlayer - there, or among the `Parameter` values of the held water-chemistry extract `data/raw/oda/kemi.csv.gz`.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-NP: The discriminator's other side is held: the water-chemistry extract carries `Nitrit+nitrat-N` on 182,399 records, `Ammoniak+ammonium-N` on 181,647, `Ortho-phosphat-P` on 192,416, `Nitrogen,total N` on 190,473 and `Phosphor, total-P` on 192,402, one result per record, so an ambient N:P can be formed by station, date and depth.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-OPTICS: The archive holds more optics than the monthly panel exposes. `docs/data/areas/stations_series.json` carries 679,422 station-months over 9 variables, of which one is optical: `fluo`, fluorescence in the relative unit `rel`, on 60,460 station-months. Beside fluorescence the raw CTD file carries the three optical channels the metric below uses: `Lysdæmpning`, light attenuation, on 5,217,377 records, `Turbiditet` on 1,076,915, and `FDOM`, the fluorescence of dissolved organic matter, on 890,921, from 2021 to 2026 only.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-PATH: A transmission becomes a coefficient only through the path length the light travelled, and no column of the extract records one.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-PCT: **First, R has no physical units.** The unit column `Enhed` holds `pct` on 11,815,696 records - exactly as many as `Lysdæmpning` (5,217,377) and `Oxygenmætning` (6,598,319) carry together - and none of its units is a coefficient per metre: the attenuation channel is a percentage transmission, not an attenuation coefficient.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-PROXY: An optical proxy for them means detecting, inside a residual, a substance that is counted by staining because it is otherwise transparent. Aggregated gel does scatter - TEP form the aggregates known as marine snow - but turbidity is a measure of scattered light, and it is subtracted out before R is formed.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-SEARCHED: The source register's `J1-J2-J3-GAP` records searches of PANGAEA, HELCOM's catalogue, Dryad, Zenodo and the ODA parameter lists that found no Danish TEP, sea-surface microlayer or surfactant measurement either.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-SHRINK: `RESIDUAL.md` gives the test such a number must pass: **R must shrink by exactly P when a part P is measured out of it.**
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-SMALL: **30 Alcian-blue TEP samples from the rosette on casts already running the four-sensor suite, at stations carrying FDOM.** Not a survey - a calibration: the paired points settle whether R carries any TEP information. A correlation would turn the existing four-sensor casts into a retrospective TEP series; no correlation retires the optical route. The method needs the dye and a spectrophotometer.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-START: **Third, even the ship's own attenuation coefficient depends on how the cast was taken.** In this project's light analysis the growth-season casts whose profile begins above 2 m give a median Kd of 0.35 and those beginning below it 0.27; where a cast starts is a matter of how it was taken, not of the water.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-STATUS: **Missing: measurement** - specifically *a new metric over what is already recorded*. TEP, the quantity the hypothesis is about, is recorded in nothing held here. A metric over the optics already recorded can be written down; it cannot be formed in physical units, and if it could it could not be attributed to gel.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-TRANSP: **And the target's own name is the last objection.** TEP are, in the encyclopaedia's words, *otherwise transparent*: they are counted by staining them with Alcian blue.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-TWOUNITS: That the column mixes scales is visible in the same table: `Konduktivitet`'s 5,169,432 records are exactly the 4,425,685 in `mS/cm` and the 743,747 in `mS/m`, and `Vægtfylde`'s 4,329,674 exactly the 3,412,290 in `g/l` and the 917,384 in `kg/m3`: one parameter, two unit labels, told apart only by the unit field of each record.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-UNSCOREABLE: The hypothesis is missing its dependent variable, not its discriminator. **Absent dimension: J1 is unscoreable, not refuted.**
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-VACUOUS: **Second, the shrink-by-P test is vacuous, because P is fitted rather than measured.** Adding FDOM does reduce R - but FDOM's *contribution to attenuation* is the fitted coefficient of the same regression that produces R, not an independent measurement of it. The account is circular in the way `RESIDUAL.md` describes, and `R_new = R_old − P` has no independent `P`. It would become a real test only if the absorption by dissolved matter were measured, and none of the extract's channels measures an absorption.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-WOULD: It **would** license a description: how much attenuation is unexplained by the three channels meant to explain it, in ranks rather than units, and whether that share has seasonal or station shape.
openproblems/J1.md.C-OQ-J1-WOULDNOT: It **would not** license calling the residual gel, TEP or fedtemøg. That is the shrinkage move in `RESIDUAL.md` - naming the leftover after one item on its list - and the list here includes the sondes' calibration, which the extract corrects by a factor other than one on 2,813,137 records, the unrecorded path length, dissolved matter FDOM does not see, and whatever else attenuates light that none of the three channels measures.

openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-ABSENT: **Still absent from anything found:** a paired sequential iron *and* sulphur extraction (AVS, CRS, ascorbate/dithionite iron) on Danish sediment.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-AL561: **AL561** (GEOMAR, 2021; PANGAEA `987329`–`987366`): sediment cores and benthic landers at high-accumulation sites in the Skagerrak and Kattegat; the chamber record at station `AL561_17-1` lists phosphate among its measured nutrients.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-AL561-FES: The source register records the cruise's sulphur as bulk total sulphur and its iron as dissolved porewater iron, not a sequential extraction, so the Fe:S ratio R6 needs cannot be computed from it.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-CENSOR: **Censoring.** Where the oxidised zone is deep, the added sediment can consume all the H₂S added (≈ 100 µmol), and the method then reports the buffer capacity as `>x µmol cm-2`: right-censored precisely at the high-iron stations R6 cares most about.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-CLASS: **Missing: experiment, constructive.** R6's discriminator is a *rate* against a *ratio* - sediment Fe:S and Fe:P against phosphate release rate - and its causal clause is comparative: marine sediment releases more phosphate under anoxia *because of the sulphate*. A field record varies sulphate only together with salinity, organic loading, iron supply and temperature, so the contrast has to be built, in a core incubation.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-CONFOUND: A correlation between bed oxygen and water-column phosphate is equally predicted by A7, R2, R5 and plain mineralisation. **Unscoreable here, not refuted.**
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-CONSUMED: The report reads the two seasonal changes as of the same order - iron consumed as the sulphide front advances, in Danish sediment, seasonally - while noting that other substances than oxidised iron add to the buffer capacity and that the iron was measured only near the surface.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-DOME: **ICES DOME**'s Danish sediment contaminant file is an open download, fed from Danish monitoring and so not a separate production path. This project's reading of it is a note in the source register, from an analysis not stored as a script, and the note does not say whether iron, sulphur and phosphorus were measured on the same samples.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-ENDPOINT: It is also the wrong side of the mechanism: **free sulphide in the water column is what remains after the sediment's iron buffer is spent**, a detector of the endpoint, not of the process.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-FLUXDATA: The measurements behind it were not found in any reachable dataset.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-FLUXES: The 1998 method specifies core-incubation phosphate fluxes, and DCE's SR323 tabulates a seasonal internal load of DIN and DIP for Roskilde, Odense, Horsens and Ringkøbing Fjord from summer 1999 to spring 2000, credited to unpublished data.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-H2S: **The `Dihydrogensulfid` series, checked rather than assumed.** The CTD extract's `Dihydrogensulfid` has 2,601 records at 4 stations, 2,598 of them from station `93610032` in Mariager Fjord.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-H2SUSE: One silled fjord whose inner basin exchanges little water: usable for the H₂S climatology of Mariager Fjord's bottom water and nothing comparative.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-KEMIH2S: The held water-chemistry extract carries sulphide from bottles under two names, `Dihydrogensulfid` on 1,188 records and `Svovlbrinte (sulfid)` on 621: a separate production path, measuring the same endpoint.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-LICENSE: A successful incubation licenses one narrow thing: *in this sediment, sulphate availability changes phosphate release per unit mineralisation by this factor*. It would **not** license a Danish phosphorus budget, a water-body allocation, or a claim about the Baltic feedback - one sediment is one sediment, and R6's unit is depositional history, not a map. Nor the freshwater comparison R6 makes in words: that needs the same dose series on lake sediment, and Danish lake and marine sediments differ in much more than sulphate. The honest limit is that it tests the *step* - sulphide strips iron, iron was holding phosphate - not the *system claim* that this is what makes the marine case worse.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-METHOD: The 1998 method specifies the buffer capacity as a titration of the sulphide-free surface sediment with H₂S, reported as µmol of H₂S consumed per cm², and measures oxidised iron in the same zone so the two can be related: a *functional assay of the reactive iron pool* R6 turns on.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-NOVANA: The national programme for 2023–2027 takes, in sediment, total N, total P, iron-bound phosphate, dry matter, loss on ignition and density, in layers of the top 10 cm, once a year, when the sediment is most oxidised, in January–February.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-NOVANA-NOBUF: Neither the sulphide front, the buffer capacity nor oxidised iron is in its text.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-NULL: The naive null - "anoxic sediment releases no more phosphate than oxic sediment" - is wrong, and would hand R6 a win it has not earned: under anoxia phosphate is released by the breakdown of organic matter, and iron-reducing bacteria free iron-bound phosphate, whether or not sulphide forms.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-NULL2: The constraint an incubation imposes is *same sediment, same anoxia, sulphate varied*. So the null is **equality of phosphate release per unit mineralisation across sulphate levels** - flux(PO₄³⁻) normalised to concurrent flux(DIC) or NH₄⁺ from the same core, sulphate the only manipulated term. Under `H0` that ratio is flat in sulphate; R6 predicts it rises and saturates where reactive iron is exhausted. A design without a sulphate-free *anoxic* arm cannot reject anything, however many replicates it has.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-ODASED: **ODA `Sedimentkemi/Sporstof`** (`Emne_12_19`): the source register records its parameters - loss on ignition, total N, iron-adsorbed P, total P, dry matter and density, none of them an iron content - and the portal's station list at 18 stations with no period set and 39 over the whole record. It is not held here.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-PANEL: The archive's finest routine observable near the bed is a monthly median per station: `stations_series.json` holds 679,422 station-months at 1,415 stations over 564 months from 1980, near-bed oxygen on 76,980 of them.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-PG880132: **PANGAEA `880132`**: sequential phosphorus extraction, iron-bound phosphorus among its fractions, on one sediment core from the Bornholm Basin.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-PG997075: **PANGAEA `997075`**: Kiel Bight sediment cores collected in February 2025 and incubated under controlled oxygen cycles, with sequential iron extraction, total sulphur, hydrogen sulphide, sulphate, ammonium, alkalinity and sulphate reduction rates by radiotracer; from GEOMAR, a production path separate from Danish monitoring.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-PG997075-NOP: Its record lists no phosphorus measurement.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-RESULTS: DCE's SR323 reports from it, as means over the areas: the front rose from 51 mm below the surface in spring to 25 mm in autumn, and the buffer capacity fell from 29 to 15 µmol cm⁻²; its figure's bars give the spread over 1998–2003. Oxidised iron in the top 1.5 cm ranged from 2 to 2,741 µmol, with geometric means of 9.3 in spring and 2.0 in autumn once Limfjorden and Ringkøbing Fjord are set aside.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-S1: **Run the 1998 assay at 20 existing `Bundfauna` stations, one spring and one autumn.** Silver-plate front, buffer capacity, oxidised iron, beside the iron-adsorbed phosphorus `Sedimentkemi` already carries. Report the censoring threshold with every `>` value. Cost: a protocol that already exists in Danish, a syringe and a photometer.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-S2: **The incubation.** One Danish sediment, homogenised, split across a sulphate dose series from 1 to 28 mM at fixed ionic strength by NaCl substitution, so *sulphate* is the treatment. Track PO₄³⁻, DIC/NH₄⁺, H₂S and sulphate reduction rate in the overlying water; sequential iron (ascorbate/dithionite) and sulphur (AVS/CRS) on the cores at the end.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-S2B: PANGAEA `997075` makes sulphate, sulphide, ammonium, sulphate-reduction and sequential-iron measurements together on Kiel Bight sediment in 2025; it names no phosphorus measurement, and phosphorus is the whole of R6.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-S3: **Reclassification test, stated in advance.** If the NOVA-era rows (front, buffer, oxidised iron, 1998–2003) are recoverable from the former county archives at ≥10 stations with ≥4 paired seasons *and* a co-located iron-adsorbed phosphorus value, R6's **state** half becomes **armchair** and this page is half wrong. The **rate** half stays experimental regardless.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-SCALE: R6 lives at the sulphide front, which the national sediment reports place millimetres to centimetres below the sediment surface; a station-month median of bottom-water oxygen is far coarser in space and time, and the wrong quantity besides: oxygen is R6's *precondition*, not its consequence.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-SR323: **DCE's SR323**, *Sammenhænge i det marine miljø* (`dce2.au.dk/pub/SR323.pdf`), analyses the national sediment programme: loss on ignition, total N, total P and iron-bound P in the top 10 cm at 12 stations measured both in 1999–2003 and in 2017–2018, in 7 Danish fjord areas, the Sydfynske Øhav and northern Øresund; the sulphide front and buffer capacity in 16 areas, spring and autumn; and, in open waters from 2005 to 2015, sulphide at 16 of 20 stations.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-STATE: Running the 1998 assay would give iron and sulphur as *state variables* - worth doing, and only a measurement problem. It still would not test R6, which asserts a **causal dependence of phosphate release on sulphate**, and the field never varies sulphate alone.
openproblems/R6.md.C-OQ-R6-TA14: **NOVA teknisk anvisning `kap. 14`** (1998), the national method: the sulphide front by silver plate (`§14.7.1.1`), the sulphide buffer capacity (`§14.7.1.2`), oxidised iron in the buffer zone (`§14.7.1.3`), iron-bound phosphorus (`§14.6.1.1`), and the fluxes of oxygen and nutrients, ortho-phosphate among them, between incubated cores and the water above them (`§14.8`).
